subject: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@galaxyapps.com>, procurement@galaxyapps.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Feb 2027 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Hi Laura / procurement team,

Following up on the renewal alert we received for GalaxyApps (coming up in March). I know you opened a bake-off with FastCompute — thanks for keeping us in the loop. From the usage patterns we see, your March renewal looks like a good point to formalize a migration/playbook that covers: a short parallel run, a capacity uplift for the spring campaign (estimate ~1.5x current peak), and an operational rollback plan.

I attached a short proposed MAP (mutual action plan) and a preliminary SLA/terms doc to kick off internal review. Key asks from my side: can you confirm the target date window for the migration and the expected surge dates? Also, if FastCompute shared any raw benchmarks, please forward those so we can do a side-by-side.

Suggested next step: 30-min sync this week (I have Thu/Fri morning PST open).

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed-MAP.xlsx (Mutual action plan, milestones)

From: Laura Chen <laura@galaxyapps.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@galaxyapps.com, cto@galaxyapps.com
Date: Thu, 04 Feb 2027 10:02:13 -0800
Subject: Re: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Hannah — thanks for the outreach. We are under pressure to reduce per-token spend and get a demonstrable latency improvement for our chat flows. FastCompute ran a short bake-off last week and their summary suggests lower median latency at our typical seq lengths; I attached their summary for reference.

Questions up-front:
- Can Redwood match or improve on the latencies they reported?
- We need a guaranteed plan for a 1.5x peak capacity for our spring campaign (two-week window in April).
- What sort of migration credits/discounts do you offer if there is an outage or performance delta?

I'll loop in our CTO to weigh in on technical questions — can Ben join the next call?

Laura Chen
Head of Product, GalaxyApps
Attachment: fastcompute-bench-summary.pdf

> Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@galaxyapps.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 14:24:36 -0800
Subject: Re: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Laura — appreciate the context. I ran a targeted comparison using your payload profiles and a short prefix cache test; attached is a 6-page summary (redwood-bakeoff-results.pdf) with raw P95/P50 numbers and cost per 1k tokens assuming similar batching. High-level:
- Median latency: Redwood 85ms vs FastCompute 78ms at 1 concurrent request baseline (difference driven by FastCompute's optimized kernel for short sequences).
- P95 latency: Redwood 220ms vs FastCompute 260ms (our continuous batching and KV cache help at tail).
- Unit cost: Redwood slightly lower at current config when prefix caching enabled (projected 7–12% savings).

Recommendation: For your 1.5x surge window we should provision a small Dedicated pool (single-instance scale set) for the two-week peak; that gives predictable throughput and isolation during the campaign. We can also offer a short free dedicated pilot (7 days) to run your real traffic and validate tail metrics. If you want, we can run the pilot as a canary against your production percentage.

Next steps I propose:
1) Set up a 7-day dedicated pilot for the April window.
2) We provide a written offer for a 12-month reserved capacity with an upsell allowance and a migration credit if service-level targets aren’t met during the cutover.
3) Tech sync with your CTO to agree measurement queries and acceptability thresholds (P95 target, error budget).

I’ll attach the detailed results and a proposed MAP with milestone owners.

—Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-results.pdf, proposed-MAP.xlsx

From: procurement@galaxyapps.com <procurement@galaxyapps.com>

Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Hannah / Marissa —

Thank you for the materials. A few procurement/legal questions before we proceed to a pilot:
- Contract length: we prefer 24 months but will consider 12 months if pricing is favorable.
- For the dedicated pool, we need clear SLAs and credits for unplanned downtime.
- Can you confirm pricing for the 1.5x temporary uplift (per-hour rate) and how that interacts with committed capacity discounts?

Please include your legal contact and the exact DocuSign flow in the next email.

Regards,
GalaxyApps Procurement

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: procurement@galaxyapps.com, laura@galaxyapps.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 11:43:05 -0800
Subject: Re: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Procurement / Laura —

Thanks for the concrete asks. We've reviewed this with L4 and the commercial team. Approved commercial outline below (binding terms to follow in a formal SOW):

- Contract term: 12 months (preferred by Redwood for pilot + committed pricing), with option to extend to 24 months at a pre-agreed renewal rate.
- Dedicated capacity pricing: 20% discount on top of standard reserved rates for commitments above 50k compute-hours/month.
- Surge uplift: flat per-hour uplift rate for the two-week window; if you commit to the reserved threshold we will cap surge billing to 10% above the committed monthly spend for that month.
- Migration credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of first-month committed spend if SLA targets (P95 latency and error budget) are missed during the migration window.

Attached is a formal offer summary (redwood-offer-terms.pdf) and the updated MAP. Legal contact: contracts@redwood.com (I will ask legal to prepare the SOW and DocuSign envelope).

If that looks ok, Hannah will share the DocuSign link once legal drops the envelope. We can also provision the pilot the week before your spring campaign to run a non-zero percentage of traffic through Redwood for validation.

—Marissa Cole
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-offer-terms.pdf

From: Laura Chen <laura@galaxyapps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@galaxyapps.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, cto@galaxyapps.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GalaxyApps renewal: migration playbook & capacity shift

Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the concrete terms. The commercial outline looks reasonable; I have two asks before we route to legal:
1) Please include an explicit performance measurement clause that defines the P95 measurement window and the metrics we will use for the migration credit calculation.
2) Provide a draft DocuSign link for the 12-month pilot offer so procurement can sign and lock dates.

If you can get contracts@redwood.com to send the envelope today we will prioritize internal approval and loop our legal. Once signed, we'll schedule the pilot and assign an internal run owner.

Laura Chen
Head of Product, GalaxyApps
